correctness.rationale: A dominating m-by-m rook placement must meet every row or every column; a size-m placement therefore chooses exactly one in each row or each column. Within a row-once set the induced graph consists of column cliques; it has a perfect matching exactly when all occupancies are even. This proves both directions, disjointness, the exact multinomial generating function and the sharp cardinality bound. Moving two occupants from one even column to another gives paths within each orientation for r>=2. A cross-orientation pair shares at most h cells because any occupied column of the row type has at least two occupants, forcing r>=h; the displayed S,T attain overlap h. Independently enumerated all 4-by-4 rook subsets through cardinality 4, recovered 80 valid minima (40 each type), zero batch-one edges and full batch-two connectivity; independent even-fiber n=4,6 scripts and checks of coefficient n=8 are supplementary, not infinite proof. The proof covers all stated even m, including m=4 where 2<=r<h is empty.

value.rationale: Even rook graphs form a canonical Cartesian-product family and their paired-dominating optima have nontrivial parity geometry. Complete classification and enumeration plus the sharp h=m/2 global reconfiguration threshold distinguish two-coordinate changes sufficient within each orientation from coordination linear in m needed to connect orientations. This is a natural all-order structural result, not a small-graph statistic.
